Frontend UI verified via Playwright as admin 9513242807/Repro@123: dashboard shows KPI row (Projects/Team Members/Procurement Queue/Procurement Paid) and NO 'Consolidated · All Projects' card; each ProjectPivot table has exactly two columns 'Component' and 'Sold (booked)' — no 'All plots' column. Each card shows Total plots / Sold stats and TeamRow chips: Admin='Debabrata', Process Admin='—' (no post_sales user exists — correct behaviour). design_issues.screen: SellDialog — Sale date & row Due date
issues: Uses browser-native HTML5 <input type='date'> which renders inconsistently across Chromium/Firefox/Safari and shows an OS-specific popup. Consider a shadcn/react-day-picker Calendar for a consistent look and to match the app's design system.

design_issues.screen: SellDialog — On Offer of Possession checkbox
issues: When 'On Offer of Possession' is toggled ON, the date input is replaced with a static label but the checkbox stays visible directly below — visually the toggle-off affordance is small; consider swapping to a segmented control (Date | On possession).

Both cards show 'Process Admin —' because no post_sales user exists yet. This is correct behaviour but the empty-state '—' pill is easy to miss; consider a hint like 'Invite a Process Admin from Team' to guide the admin.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1665 lines — still overdue for modular split (projects/units/sales/procurement/accounts/files/dashboards).
PATCH /projects/{id}/rate accepts any float including negatives (e.g. -1000) — no validation. Add `ge=0` on RateUpdate.rate_per_sqft or reject negative values.

SellUnitRequest.buyer_name defaults to '' (Optional[str]='') but sell_unit stores it verbatim; downstream code (search, sales UI sublabel) already handles empty strings, but the sale_recorded notification message uses `f'{buyer_name} · '` only when truthy — good, but consider persisting `None` instead of '' to distinguish 'walk-in / unknown' from 'not yet captured'.

In Projects.jsx ProjectCard, when p.rate_per_sqft is 0 the Save button is enabled the moment the user types then clears the field (rate='' → Number('')=0 → dirty=false relative to 0, ok). But typing 0 into a project that already has rate 0 still allows Save (dirty is false so button disables — correct). Small nit: no min=0 on the input; users can type -50 and click Save (server accepts it — see previous point).

Units.jsx ProjectInventory computes plcCols with regex /plc/i on column labels. This is brittle — a future column labelled e.g. 'Special Placement' could accidentally match. Consider a dedicated tag like 'plc' or a boolean flag on Project.columns entries.

SellDialog's schedule validation `!r.amount || (!r.due_date && !r.on_possession)` allows amount=0 to slip through as truthy-fail (0 is falsy → returns error 'Each row needs...'). Fine, but the error text says 'needs an amount and a due date' when it's really 'needs a POSITIVE amount'. Consider checking Number(r.amount) > 0 explicitly.

GET /dashboard `by_project[].sold` is computed but the client also filters units.status==='sold' on Units.jsx for the per-project header — two independent implementations of 'sold count' that can drift. Prefer using the dashboard's count in Units page too.

AdminDashboard ProjectPivot renders `pv.sum_sold` right-aligned as inr(); since 0 sold across the app, all rows print '₹0.00' — visually noisy. Consider dimming zeroes or hiding rows where `sum_sold==0 && tag !== 'total'`.

The stale sale_recorded notification found in DB during cleanup ('Sale recorded · Plot 1 · ₹5,000,000') was NOT from this iteration — appears to be leftover from a prior test run whose cleanup regex missed. I purged it. Recommend future tests store the notification_id on creation and delete by id, not by message regex, to make cleanup deterministic.
